title: Legal Forwarding Agreements — Criteria for Forwarding an Account and Opening a Matter
content:
**Legal intake standard.** Under the Legal Forwarding Agreements, an account is forwarded to a collection attorney as a matter with the creditor client's authorization; the matter is recorded with the attorney's matter file number, the authorization date and the balance authorized for suit. The criteria below decide whether a matter may be opened.

## Standard

1. Matters are opened only under a Legal Forwarding Agreement whose status is active.
2. An account is forwarded only when all of the following hold:
   - its placement stage is on the programme's list of eligible placement stages;
   - its debt type is on the programme's list of eligible debt types;
   - it is not in dispute hold, not in hardship hold and not in a terminal status;
   - the number of open matters under the agreement is below the programme's open-matter limit per agreement.
3. A suit matter also needs:
   - a balance due on the account between the programme's smallest and largest balance due for suit, each figure itself included; and
   - at least the programme's required number of calendar days between the authorization date and the account's statute-of-limitations expiry date.
   A debt past its statute-of-limitations expiry date is never sued on.
4. A suit on a balance above the programme's preauthorized suit limit needs the client's account-level authorization, recorded as the client's authorization reference on the matter. A suit on a balance at or below that limit is a preauthorized suit and the authorization reference is left empty.
5. Each account is open in at most one matter at a time.

## Terms used in the standard

- **Open matters under the agreement** — on the handling date, the number of matters authorized under the agreement for which no closure has been recorded under the same matter file number. A closed matter does not count.
- **Agreement status** — the status Ridgeline's records show for the client's Legal Forwarding Agreement; pending signature, suspended and terminated agreements are not active.
- **Account facts** — the stage, debt type, status, balance due and statute-of-limitations expiry date are those shown on the placed account in Ridgeline's records.

## Checklist of conditions

| Condition | Applies to | Met when |
|---|---|---|
| Agreement active | every matter | the agreement's status is active |
| Stage eligible | every forwarding | the account's stage is on the programme's list |
| Debt type eligible | every forwarding | the account's debt type is on the programme's list |
| Account status | every forwarding | not dispute hold, not hardship hold, not terminal |
| Room under the limit | every forwarding | open matters are below the limit |
| Balance in range | suit matters | balance due from the smallest to the largest figure, both included |
| Limitation days | suit matters | days from authorization date to expiry date at least the required number |
| Account-level authorization | suits above the preauthorized limit | the client's authorization is recorded |
| One open matter | every account | the account has no other open matter |

Each line is a necessary condition of the standard; where any line that applies fails, the matter is not opened.

## Worked cases on hypothetical figures

The limits and dates below are invented to show how the conditions are measured.

**Open-matter limit.** Under a hypothetical limit of 25: an agreement with 24 open matters is below the limit, so this condition is met; with 25 open matters it is not below the limit, so this condition is not met. Matters already closed are not counted.

**Limitation days.** With a hypothetical requirement of 180 days and a statute-of-limitations expiry date of 30 June 2026:

| Authorization date | Calendar days to 30 June 2026 | Requirement of 180 met? |
|---|---|---|
| 1 January 2026 | 180 | Yes — exactly 180 is at least 180 |
| 2 January 2026 | 179 | No |

**Preauthorized limit.** Under a hypothetical preauthorized suit limit of $2500.00, a suit on a balance of $2500.00 needs no account-level authorization; a suit on $2500.01 needs the client's authorization, recorded as its authorization reference.

**Account status.** A bank card account at an eligible stage that is in dispute hold is not forwarded, whatever its balance.
